serum NCA is more sensitive than plasma histamine or serum ECP in detecting early and late airways responses to allergen inhalations in asthmatic patients.
the increase in serum NCA is the most sensitive marker of EAR, and that its increase during EAR is predictive of the severity and the occurrence of LAR in asthmatic patients.

the relationship between the increase of blood markers of activation of mast cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils during EAR and LARS to allergen inhalations, and the relationship between changes in these markers and the functional response.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between the increase of blood markers of mast cell and eosinophil activation and the severity of early and late asthmatic responses is complex and requires further investigation.
the increase of serum NCA during EAR is the most sensitive and specific marker of EAR and of LAR in asthmatic patients.
blood mediators of mast‐cell and eosinophil activation are not reliable markers of the severity of EAR and L AR, but that NCA increase during EAR may predict LAR severity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma histamine and NCA are useful markers to detect the presence of EAR and L AR, and that NCA increase during EAR seems to predict the severity of subsequent LAR.
blood mediators of EAR and LER are not predictive of LAR.
the increase in plasma histamine during EAR and the increase in serum NCA and ECP during LAR are the most useful markers to detect the severity of airway responses to inhaled allergen in asthematics.
